startup.name: Clara
startup.description: Clara is an AI primary care and longevity practice from the team that founded and grew Circle Medical to 100M dollars in revenue. An AI with clinical knowledge sees the patient's medical data and acts: symptom help, refills, labs and goals, with human providers reviewing recommendations. Nine people in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only: already accepted to YC Spring 2026. Prior of about 1 percent for a random applicant is not informative, so the work is in the ladder.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable because the company was accepted. A reviewer would most plausibly worry about regulation and liability for AI medical advice, and a crowded field of funded AI doctors. Because acceptance is already a fact in this test, the estimate is a placeholder and the forecast value sits in the funding ladder that follows.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed stalls only if regulators or malpractice insurers block autonomous AI care, or if investors see Doctronic and Counsel Health as too far ahead. Even so, the founders' track record makes a round likely; Prana, a similar W26 company, shows peers still waiting. Investors at this step want proof that growth, retention and margins hold up against better funded rivals, and a weak showing on any of them ends the path here, as the analogs listed in this evaluation show.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if patient growth stays slow because consumer care needs paid acquisition, or if clinical safety events or regulation limit scope. Unit economics with human review are tough, and Legion Health and Prana show that AI care companies take years to raise. Investors at this step want proof that growth, retention and margins hold up against better funded rivals, and a weak showing on any of them ends the path here, as the analogs listed in this evaluation show.

outcomes.why_it_fails: A failure would come from regulation or liability limits on AI care, or from consumer acquisition costs that outrun revenue. A small exit is plausible by sale to a larger health system or telehealth group. A meaningful exit needs a durable lead in a category where rivals can copy features and raise more money, and most companies in the reference cohort stay small, are acquired cheaply or stop operating before that point.

killers.risk: Regulation and liability for AI medical advice
killers.evidence: Utah created a sandbox for AI renewals only in 2026 and elsewhere licensing rules limit autonomous AI care.
killers.mitigation: Keep human review and operate in states that allow pilots.

killers.evidence: Doctronic raised 20M in 2025 and a 40M Series B in March 2026; Counsel Health raised 25M.
killers.mitigation: Use founder experience to build trusted clinical operations and longevity care.

killers.risk: Consumer acquisition cost and thin margins
killers.evidence: Consumer primary care needs paid acquisition and licensed clinicians, which strain unit economics.
killers.mitigation: Sell through employers and payers and automate clinician review.

technical_complexity.rationale: The AI layer is buildable on foundation models, but safety, integration with medical records, labs and prescribing, and clinical workflows are hard and regulated. A small team can launch quickly but not prove safety fast.

takeover_risk.rationale: Funded peers and model labs can add similar features within a year, but care delivery and licensing slow copies; the founders' clinical operations experience is the moat.

evidence.claim: Utah began allowing AI to renew prescriptions in January 2026, showing regulatory and market movement.
Doctronic and Counsel Health raised large rounds for AI first care.

actions: Serve first patients with clinician review
roadmap.proof: Hundreds of active patients with low escalation errors.

pros.point: Founders built Circle Medical to 100M dollars revenue.
AI care has regulatory momentum and investor capital.

brand.name: Clara
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Clara" --era 2022+: 5 characters, 2 syllables, real word
strengths: Warm, human, easy to spell and say
weaknesses: Very common name that is hard to own in search
brand.rationale: A human first name suits a care assistant, like consumer health brands that use personas, and trust matters in medicine; common names are hard to defend legally but help warmth.

narrative.headline: The strongest founder story in a hot, regulated category; seed is very likely and Series A is a real possibility.
narrative.general_summary: Clara is an AI primary care practice from the founders of Circle Medical, which gives it unusual credibility with investors and clinicians. Peers like Doctronic and Counsel Health have raised large rounds, so capital for the category is available. The risks are regulation, liability, a crowded field and the cost of acquiring patients. A seed is very likely and later rounds depend on safety data and unit economics. The forecast treats the day one description as the best case, anchors on the 2022 to 2024 cohort of researched YC companies, and widens the uncertainty because funding data for recent batches is incomplete and right censored.
